study_design_verbatim.value: We randomly assigned 25 morbidly obese adult tracheotomized subjects ... to 1 of 2 methods of setting PEEP; using either titration guided by esophageal balloon to overcome negative transpulmonary pressure (Ptp) (goal Ptp 0-5 cmH2O) (ESO group) or titration to maximize static effective lung compliance (Cstat group).

provenance.quote: We randomly assigned 25 morbidly obese adult tracheotomized subjects (median [interquartile range] BMI 53.4 [26.4]; range 40.4-113.8) to 1 of 2 methods of setting PEEP; using either titration guided by esophageal balloon to overcome negative transpulmonary pressure (Ptp) (goal Ptp 0-5 cmH2O) (ESO group) or titration to maximize static effective lung compliance (Cstat group).
due to the nature of our intervention, our study could not be blinded to either the subjects or the therapists
The study was conducted in a university teaching hospital with a 9-bed respiratory intermediate unit (RIU).

inclusion_criteria.value: Tracheotomized morbidly obese adult subjects (body mass index [BMI] ≥ 40; age > 18 years) with recent admission to the intensive care unit, for non-ARDS hypoxic and/or hypercapnic respiratory failure with need for intubation and mechanical ventilation, with subsequent tracheostomy creation for failure to liberate from the ventilator were enrolled if they had failed at least one post-tracheostomy weaning attempt during their index hospitalization. exclusion_criteria.value: Subjects were excluded if there was any active lung, neuromuscular, or cardiac disease that would preclude ventilator weaning. comparator_verbatim.value: Subjects randomized to the Cstat group had PEEP adjusted to achieve the best static effective compliance (Cstat) as automatically calculated and displayed on the graphic interface of the Hamilton G5 or Galileo ventilator. Positive end-expiratory pressure was adjusted in increments of 3 cmH2O until there was a less than 5% observed improvement in the measured Cstat averaged over 5 breaths. The PEEP with the best achieved Cstat was chosen.

outcomes.name_verbatim: Percentage of subjects weaned from the ventilator at day 30
outcomes.definition_verbatim: A subject was considered successfully weaned if spontaneously breathing without ventilator support for at least 24 hours by day 30. Subjects who required resumption of mechanical ventilation after an initial liberation were presumed to have failed if they were still on the ventilator by day 30.

provenance.quote: 8/13 subjects (62%) in the ESO Group were weaned vs. 9/12(75%) in the Cstat Group (P = 0.67).

With respect to our study group, there was no significant between group difference in the percentage of subjects weaned by day 30. Eight subjects (62%) were weaned in the ESO group vs 9 (75%) in the Cstat group (P = .67).

outcomes.name_verbatim: Time to wean from mechanical ventilation (among successfully weaned subjects)
outcomes.definition_verbatim: The time to wean was measured from the date of randomization to the date of liberation from mechanical ventilation.

provenance.quote: Subjects in the ESO group weaned in a median of 3.5 days (range 1-16 days)
a median of 14 days (range 7-26 days) for subjects in the Cstat group (P = .012)
Among the 17 subjects who weaned, median time to ventilator liberation was significantly shorter in the ESO group: 3.5 days vs Cstat group 14 days (P = .01).

Among the 17 subjects who successfully weaned, subjects in the ESO group weaned significantly quicker than those in the Cstat group. Subjects in the ESO group weaned in a median of 3.5 days vs 14 days for subjects in the Cstat group (P = .012; Figure 1).

outcomes.name_verbatim: Time to achieve ventilator independence (entire cohort)

When the time to wean data were analyzed in the entire cohort (N = 25) using survival analysis, we found that the greatest impact to weaning using esophageal balloon was seen in the first 15 days. If subjects were not weaned by day 15, the outcome was the same as in the Cstat group (Figure 2).

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ARDS was an exclusion criterion, so ards_subgroup is non_ards. Enrolment required BMI ≥ 40, so obesity_subgroup is obese_population. Timing_subgroup is unclear because the reference event is enrolment, and the time from ICU admission/intubation to enrolment is not reported.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: No matching trial registration, enrolment period, or centre found in other reports in the pool. This is a single-centre study from East Carolina University/Vidant Medical Center, not listed in COHORTS.md.
unclear_items: n_analysed: The paper states that two subjects with very early protocol violations were excluded from the intention-to-treat population, but the tables show N=13 and N=12, summing to 25. This discrepancy is unresolved.
The postadjustment timepoint is not precisely defined; it likely refers to after initial PEEP optimization on study day 1, but the exact timing is not specified.
The abstract reports optimal PEEP as 26.5 ± 5.7 cmH2O (ESO) and 24.2 ± 7.0 cmH2O (Cstat), while Table 2 and Table 3 report 27 ± 6 and 24 ± 7. The discrepancy is flagged.
country: USA was inferred from author affiliation (Brody School of Medicine, East Carolina University, Greenville, NC, USA).
planned_sample_size: Derived as 56 total (28 per group × 2 groups).
timing_subgroup: Reference event is enrolment; hours from ICU admission or intubation are not reported.
extraction_flags.general_notes: The study is an exploratory pilot with early termination. The primary outcome per the statistical analysis is time to wean, but the paper also reports weaning success at day 30.
